circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, the 5. 281 km Yas Marina Circuit was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for the season-closing Formula One Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One venue to be constructed, following Bahrain's circuit and preceding facilities in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street layout that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and holds an FIA Grade 1 classification. It hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year, along with the Supercars Championship's Melbourne event and various supporting race categories.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix during two separate periods, first as the Österreichring from 1970-1987 and later as the A1-Ring following its reconstruction and shortening from 1997-2003. The track underwent significant modifications between these eras before returning to host Formula One racing under its new identity.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue in Formula One. The circuit first hosted F1 racing in 2016 with the European Grand Prix, before becoming home to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: The Bahrain International Circuit, a 5. 412 km facility that opened in 2004, hosts the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, making it the venue for the sport's inaugural Middle Eastern race. Beyond Formula One, the track accommodates various racing series including GP2, drag racing, and 24-hour endurance events, while holding FIA Grade 1 certification and offering multiple circuit configurations.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of lengthy straightaways and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for competitors. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 accreditation and accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa is a 7. 004 km Belgian circuit situated in the Wallonia region near the town of Spa, serving as the home of the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The venue has maintained continuous Grand Prix racing from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary road course that hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix annually. Beyond Formula One, the track has accommodated various international racing series including sports car championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport venue is primarily recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 through 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing circuit located near villages in Northamptonshire that has hosted the British Grand Prix since 1948, making it the venue for the first-ever World Championship race in 1950. Following decades of shared hosting with other tracks, the Grand Prix became permanently based at Silverstone from 1987 onwards, and the circuit continues to stage both Formula One and MotoGP events.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held in Eastern Europe when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months, a faster construction timeline than any contemporary Grand Prix venue, the 4. 381 km circuit was established outside the city near a major road after initial plans for a street track in Budapest's central park were rejected by authorities.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 that ranks among Europe's oldest dedicated racing venues. The track hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" for its distinctive layout featuring lengthy straights and fast-paced corner sequences.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, operated by Honda Mobilityland, is a 5. 807 km Japanese racing venue situated in Mie Prefecture that hosts major international motorsport competitions. The track, with a spectator capacity of 155,000, is particularly renowned for staging Formula One and Super Formula championship races.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, running alongside the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its collection of major hotels and casinos. The track passes by several iconic venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, making it one of motorsport's most distinctive urban settings.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Mexico City's Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit named in honour of two fatal racing drivers, the Rodriguez brothers, who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The venue resumed hosting Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix from 2015 onwards, having previously staged the race during two earlier eras on an alternative configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that drivers navigate at an average qualifying speed of approximately 139 mph. Designed by specialist track architects, the circuit was created specifically to host the Miami Grand Prix, which joined the Formula One World Championship calendar starting in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track winding through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts of Monaco, circling the harbour area. Though officially named after the principality itself, it is widely known as Monte Carlo since the majority of the circuit traverses that particular neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes west of Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that rejoined Formula One's schedule in 2021 for the Dutch Grand Prix. The venue's involvement with the sport will conclude following the 2026 season.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Situated north of Doha in Qatar, Lusail International Circuit is an FIA Grade 1 facility measuring 5. 419 km with a notably long main straight of 1. 068 km.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing venue in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was later renamed after deceased Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace in 1985. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and features an associated kart facility dedicated to Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront in Jeddah. Since its debut in 2021, it has served as the permanent home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One, and recently began hosting electric racing competitions as well.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a temporary road course located in Singapore that winds around Marina Bay, incorporating sections of the Downtown Core and Kallang urban districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657-kilometer circuit near Montmeló features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas, situated in Austin, Texas, is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the United States Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including NASCAR, MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance race, while previously accommodating various other racing series.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Thai-British driver Alexander Albon currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, where he has claimed two world championships in 2005 and 2006 during his time at Renault, along with 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans wins and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both the Formula One drivers' title and the world sportscar championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli joined Mercedes for the 2025 Formula One season and has already secured six race victories during his inaugural campaign.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: British driver Oliver Bearman currently races for Haas in Formula One competition. His career has progressed through the ranks to reach the sport's premier championship level.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team, representing his nation in the sport's premier competition.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has yielded ten Grand Prix victories. He achieved the runner-up position in the drivers' championship on two occasions, both while driving for Mercedes in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve position with Haas in Formula One while competing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category for Nielsen Racing. Between 2024 and 2025, he made seven Grand Prix appearances in the sport's top category.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: French driver Pierre Gasly currently races for Alpine in Formula One. He achieved a Grand Prix victory at Monza in 2020 while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar is a Franco-Algerian driver who represents France in Formula One, currently racing for Red Bull Racing.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record-tying seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing by winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having achieved nine Grand Prix victories throughout his career. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022 while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver who has alternated between Formula One and other motorsport series, most recently competing in F1 from 2022 to 2024. Currently, he races in the FIA World Endurance Championship as a BMW factory driver for WRT, while also taking part in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver competing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Throughout his eight-season career in the sport, he has accumulated twelve Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One after previously achieving success with Alpine, where he secured victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over 15 seasons of experience and six Grand Prix victories to the grid. He achieved his strongest championship result in 2023 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings while competing for Red Bull.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian driver currently competing for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories over his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: An Australian driver who raced in Formula One over a 14-year span from 2011 through 2024, Daniel Ricciardo earned eight Grand Prix victories during his career and was known by the nickname "the Honey Badger". His racing tenure spanned multiple teams throughout this period.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell, a British driver, has competed in Formula One for eight seasons and claimed seven Grand Prix victories. He currently races for Mercedes in the championship.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant competed in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to sports car racing. He currently races in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, having previously campaigned in the IMSA SportsCar Championship's LMP2 division.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian driver currently racing in Formula One with the Aston Martin team.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese driver, held a reserve position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls during his Formula One tenure spanning 2021 to 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver races for Red Bull Racing and has secured four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across his 12 seasons in Formula One, Verstappen has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is a Chinese racing driver currently employed as a reserve driver by Cadillac in Formula One. He competed in the sport's top category between 2022 and 2024, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese driver to have raced in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based Alpine F1 team, operating under French licence, rebranded from Renault in 2021 to represent the Alpine sports car marque while maintaining works team status until Renault's 2025 departure from the sport. The team has claimed a single victory in its Alpine iteration, courtesy of Esteban Ocon's triumph at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and currently competes with Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One across multiple eras through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished team, having participated in every world championship since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The squad, colloquially referred to by their emblem's equine moniker, remains unmatched in its competitive longevity and achievements within the championship.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-based Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas, the team commenced competition in 2016 after its establishment in 2014. Leadership transitioned in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the team principal role from Guenther Steiner, who had directed operations since the squad's inception.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded in 1970 by Peter Sauber, this Swiss engineering outfit built sports cars before graduating to Formula One as an independent constructor in 1993, achieving notable success in endurance racing including a Le Mans victory. After three decades competing in the championship under various guises, the team ceased operations in 2025 as one of the sport's longest-serving constructors, with its assets subsequently acquired to form the foundation of Audi's factory F1 effort.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. As a subsidiary of the McLaren Group, the team operates from the McLaren Technology Centre.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has been a major Formula One presence since 1954, competing as both a constructor and power unit supplier at different points in its history. The current team, based in Brackley and operating under a German licence, operates as a tripartite partnership between the Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff following a 2022 restructuring. The marque's racing endeavours are famously known by the "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor established in 2024, operating as Red Bull's second factory team alongside the primary Red Bull Racing outfit. Based in Faenza with a secondary facility near Milton Keynes, the team represents Austrian conglomerate Red Bull's dual-team strategy in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that began competing in 2024 as the second team owned by Red Bull GmbH alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with an additional facility near Milton Keynes, the team operates as a sister squad within the Red Bull motorsport structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing operates as an Austrian-licensed Formula One outfit headquartered in England, representing one of two racing operations within the Red Bull GmbH portfolio. Established in 2005 and guided by Christian Horner through two decades of competition, the team transitioned leadership to Laurent Mekies in 2025 following Horner's departure.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering is a British Formula One team and constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, emerging from the collapse of Williams's prior racing venture. Based in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team competes in 2026 as Atlassian Williams F1 Team and operates from a substantial facility spanning 60 acres.
